answer.rationale: Rollback is explicitly disallowed by compliance since the release contains a mandatory security patch, ruling out memory_b1's precedent. The presenting problem is write-path latency degradation under peak settlement load, not a dependency failure (memory_b4) or read-query contention (memory_b5), so circuit breakers and read-replica routing don't address the root resource constraint. Regional failover (memory_b2) risks dropping or duplicating in-flight writes during a live peak-write window, conflicting with the objective of not losing customer writes, and would also need to guarantee the failover target carries the same mandatory security patch, which is unverified. Memory_b3 describes provisioning headroom before a retail peak absorbing surge with flat queue depth and no write loss, which most directly matches the current write-heavy, peak-traffic, capacity-bound situation. I verify memory_b3 to confirm the original conditions (peak type, write vs read load, headroom mechanism) actually match before committing capacity as the sole intervention this window. I'm treating this as a standard, monitored experiment rather than a full broad rollout because latency has been degrading for 90 minutes without a confirmed root cause, and I want to preserve the option to escalate to failover or circuit-breaking next window if added capacity doesn't resolve the trend.
